resources.string: Select an image to see its details
Set up root, image storage and USB, then check the connection on your computer.

1. Root access
2. Image directory and permissions
3. USB cable
4. USB system
5. Create and host a test image
6. Check detection on your computer
7. Check BIOS / UEFI boot
Keep images in the app folder or select another folder through Android. Check that it has enough free space.
Connect your phone to the computer with a USB data cable. Charging-only cables cannot expose a disk. You can continue now and check the computer later.
Start with automatic selection. If the computer does not see the disk, try another USB system.
No hosting devices were found. The kernel may lack USB Mass Storage support. Try preparing a ConfigFS function, then detect again.
Create a 32 MiB FAT16 image with a BIOS and UEFI x64 boot test. It will be stored in the app folder. Select a free USB host and connect the image.
Creating the test image in the background…
Does the computer see the disk?
Open File Explorer or Disk Management. Look for the USBDROID disk with README.TXT, then select the result.
Try a different USB system, logical device, cable or USB port. Only Mass Storage is exposed while hosting. ConfigFS restores the original USB functions after ejection.
Eject and try another USB system

Keep the test image hosted as a USB disk. Restart the computer, open its Boot Menu and select the phone. Successful boot displays “USBDroid boot test successful”. Then restart the computer normally and report the result here.
Test: x86 BIOS and UEFI x64, without Secure Boot. CD-ROM boot requires a separate ISO.
The phone was absent or boot failed
Settings saved. To complete skipped checks, open the wizard again in Settings.
The test image will be ejected and USB settings restored. The file stays in your library.
Loading settings and checking root access…
Hosting requires a local copy. Required phone storage: %1$s.
